The Nomos of Cryonics is a video I made

This is similar to the concept of a Rail state, but different in many ways

== Differences with a Rail state ==

* In theory all intermediate generations can have the immortal end as being their primary goal. 

== Contemporary cryonicists vs a cryonic civilization ==
Contemporary cryonicists have certain traits which many associate with cryonics. Likewise contemporary opponents of cryonics often have religious objections, or ethical objections which are not likely to come up against an established cryonics movement.

Contemporary cryonicists tend to be white men, socially progressive or libertarian, generally atheist, with high incomes and open to new ideas. They historically did not get frozen with their families

This is '''not''' reflective of who will be getting cryonics in the future. This is already changing, and this profile of a cryonicist itself may have contributed to the inability for a cryonics movement to develop

== Fyodorov ==
While many people will credit cryonics to more traditional futurists, the person who I'd say predicted cryonics and its potential nomos the best is Nikolai  Fyodorov. A russian mystic who died almost 70 years before cryonics existed.

== World divisions ==
This is similar to the concept of a Rail state, but different in many ways.

* Unless they gain immortality elsewhere, the preservation of the cryonics order is an extremely high priority for people. Eternal life can be treated as an infinite gain
** This will lead to intense conservatism. 
** Notably this will not lead to oppressive power structures or colonialism. Emphasis on social harmony means participation but staying in line
** Someone being thawed and dying is a threat to the very social order
** More socialist economics.
*The more people frozen the more likely revival is
**This will encourage generosity with providing it. If someone offers to freeze your grandpa and he takes it then suddenly it places an obligation on you. 
* Internal threats such as terrorism, violent crime, etc will be taken far more seriously. 
** Paradoxically crimes such as theft or minor assaults will be de-prioritized. Ideally even to the most unhinged criminal their payout matrix will always be skewed away from killing. 
** Criminals cannot be expected to believe in cryonics so 
* Population maintainance
** Having children to care for increasing numbers of frozen people will lead to an increasing population. 
* Technological progress
** Technological progress will likely not be overly high. It will definitely still be strongly valued but not as much as one may think for such a society. It's not a bunch of neckbeards 
* External threats
** Other societies may see the cryonic civilization as a threat since it will see its population go up orders of magnitude after revival is achieved
*** This threat is more likely to be countered by a state implementing cryonics itself
** Holy war is unlikely though aside from a possible early event. This is an ideological fantasy that quickly will fade away
** Brain drain to the cryonic civilization would be a more immediate threat.
